intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to maximize your chances of seeing the lights dance across the sky. Hot chocolate and blankets provided.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and the surreal experience of bathing outdoors in steaming 38°C waters surrounded by black lava fields. Book the Comfort package for best value.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers in a stunning rural setting. A truly local and affordable alternative.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fresh-caught Arctic char, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbor district with knowledgeable local guides.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's dramatic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The hike offers breathtaking views of obsidian lava fields, steaming vents, and vivid mineral-streaked mountains unlike anywhere else on Earth.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and baggage claim, then take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (approx. 3,500 ISK) to Reykjavik area. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront accommodation. Unpack and rest. If skies are clear, step outside briefly to scan for northern lights from the beachfront - January offers excellent aurora viewing chances.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in transit
meals.lunch: N/A - in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the Keflavik Airport cafeteria or convenience store upon arrival (budget 1,500-2,000 ISK). Alternatively, pack snacks from duty-free.

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means very limited daylight (roughly 5-6 hours). Temperatures average -1°C to 4°C. Pack warm, waterproof layers. Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) for aurora and weather forecasts. Exchange some currency or ensure your card works internationally before leaving the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a late breakfast, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront near the resort to acclimatize to Iceland's winter landscape. Enjoy the dramatic black sand or coastal scenery depending on your exact location. Sunrise is around 11:00 AM in January - don't miss the golden hour light on the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town or Reykjavik city center by local bus (Strætó bus system, approx. 490 ISK per ride) for orientation. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (free to view exterior, 1,000 ISK to climb the tower). Stroll Laugavegur Street, the main shopping street. Browse the Kolaportið flea market if open (free entry) for cheap local goods and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area by early evening. Set an aurora alarm using the Vedur app. Head to a dark spot near the resort beach for northern lights viewing - January darkness begins around 16:00, giving many hours of potential aurora visibility. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate from a nearby supermarket (Bonus or Krónan are cheapest).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort - pick up supplies from Bonus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest grocery chain). Oatmeal, bread, eggs, and skyr yogurt are affordable staples (budget 1,500 ISK for groceries).
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand in Reykjavik - Iceland's most famous budget meal, a lamb hot dog costs around 600 ISK. A true local experience.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort using supermarket groceries. Cook pasta or soup on any available kitchen facilities. Budget approximately 1,000-1,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Visit Bonus supermarket (yellow pig logo) as soon as possible to stock up on affordable groceries for self-catered meals throughout the trip. This is the single biggest money-saving strategy in Iceland. Aurora forecast check: KP index of 3 or higher with clear skies gives good viewing chances.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or low-cost self-guided Golden Circle route if you can rent a car (split costs with other travelers - check Hostelworld or Facebook groups for carpool partners). First stop: Þingvellir National Park (free entry) - walk the Almannagjá gorge where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Sunrise around 11:00 AM creates stunning light on the rift valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area (free to visit). Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes shooting water 20-30 meters high. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall (free entry) - one of Iceland's most powerful and dramatic waterfalls, partially frozen in January for extra magic.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort. Stop at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir if budget allows (approx. 3,500 ISK) - a more affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Soak in the natural hot spring pool under the dark January sky with potential aurora overhead. Return to resort for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort - skyr with granola and coffee (from supermarket supplies).
meals.lunch: Pack a packed lunch from the resort - sandwiches, fruit, and thermos of soup. Eat in the car or at a picnic bench at Þingvellir. Saves significant money versus café stops.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort. Try making Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) with affordable lamb and root vegetables from Bonus supermarket - warming and budget-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Car rental for the Golden Circle is most cost-effective when split. Budget around 8,000-12,000 ISK per day for a small car. Alternatively, join a budget group tour from Reykjavik (approx. 7,000-9,000 ISK per person) which includes transport. Roads in January require caution - check road conditions at road.is before departing. F-roads are closed in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after yesterday's full day. Sleep in, then take a relaxing walk along the beachfront. Practice aurora photography if you stayed up late the night before. Visit a local swimming pool (sundlaug) - Reykjavik's public pools are a cultural institution and cost only 1,000-1,200 ISK. Laugardalslaug is the largest with multiple hot pots at different temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjavik waterfront and Old Harbour area. Visit the free Harpa Concert Hall (exterior and lobby are free to explore - stunning geometric glass architecture). Walk to the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) - a free iconic photo spot on the waterfront. Browse the harbor area and watch fishing boats.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free cultural event - check Reykjavik's Grapevine website (grapevine.is) for free concerts, gallery openings, or community events. Many Reykjavik venues host free or low-cost evening events. Return to resort for aurora watching from the dark beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered - eggs on toast with Icelandic butter and coffee.
meals.lunch: Hlöllabátar (Subway-style Icelandic sandwich shop) in Reykjavik - filling baguette sandwiches for around 1,500-2,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort. Budget fish dish - pick up affordable cod or haddock from Bonus supermarket and pan-fry with butter and herbs. Fresh Icelandic fish at supermarket prices is excellent value.

day_by_day.notes: Iceland's public swimming pools (sundlaugar) are essential cultural experiences and double as affordable hot spring alternatives. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees. Swimwear is mandatory and showering without a swimsuit before entering is required by Icelandic custom.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (requires car or budget group tour). Depart early to maximize the limited daylight. First stop: Ytri Tunga beach (free) - famous for wild seal colony. Seals are often visible lounging on the rocks even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along Snæfellsnes to the dramatic Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (free to view from below - the glacier that Jules Verne used as the entry point in Journey to the Center of the Earth). Drive the peninsula's southern coast stopping at Arnarstapi and Hellnar sea cliffs (free) with incredible basalt rock formations and bird life. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach (free) with its ancient lifting stones.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik and the resort. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is approximately 2-3 hours from Reykjavik. Check aurora forecast for the evening - the peninsula's dark skies offer excellent northern lights viewing if you time your return drive with a high KP index.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at resort before departure - oatmeal with honey and coffee in a thermos.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the car - this is essential for Snæfellsnes as restaurants are scarce and expensive in winter. Sandwiches, hard-boiled eggs, fruit, and hot soup in a thermos.
meals.dinner: Settle for a supermarket ready meal or self-cooked dinner at resort upon return. Alternatively, if energy allows, try Reykjavik's Noodle Station for affordable Asian noodle soup (around 1,800-2,200 ISK) - a budget traveler favorite.

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day commitment - budget 10-12 hours including driving. Check road.is for winter road conditions before departing. The peninsula can have severe weather. If conditions are poor, this day can be swapped with a Reykjavik city day. A budget group tour to Snæfellsnes costs approximately 8,000-12,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and hot spring day. Visit Reykjadalur Hot Spring Thermal River (free natural hot spring) - a 3km hike each way from the trailhead near Hveragerði town. The hike takes about 45-60 minutes each way through geothermal landscape with steaming vents and bubbling mud pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the natural hot river at Reykjadalur - bring a swimsuit and change in the basic changing facilities. The water temperature varies along the river; walk upstream for hotter water. This is one of Iceland's best free hot spring experiences. Spend 1-2 hours soaking and enjoying the geothermal landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hveragerði town. Browse the small town's geothermal greenhouse bakery (Varma) for affordable fresh bread baked using geothermal heat - a unique Icelandic experience. Return to resort. Set aurora alarm and spend the evening watching for northern lights from the beachfront. January's long dark nights maximize aurora viewing windows.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort before the hike - high-energy breakfast of oatmeal, skyr, and fruit.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch to enjoy at the hot river - sandwiches and snacks. Eating by a steaming geothermal river in January is a memorable experience.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer self-cooked meal - Icelandic lamb chops from Bonus supermarket with roasted root vegetables.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjadalur hike can be icy and slippery in January - bring hiking poles if possible and wear waterproof boots with good grip. The hike is moderate difficulty. Hveragerði is about 45 minutes from Reykjavik by bus (Strætó route 51, approx. 1,000 ISK). Bring a dry bag for your phone and valuables near the hot spring.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint of the trip - explore Reykjavik's free museums and cultural sites. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) - free on specific days or approx. 2,500 ISK. Alternatively, the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) at 2,200 ISK offers fascinating Viking age archaeology built around a real 10th-century longhouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to Perlan (The Pearl) - the futuristic dome building on Öskjuhlíð hill. The observation deck has panoramic 360° views over Reykjavik (free to walk up the hill, small fee for inside exhibits). Explore the surrounding Öskjuhlíð forest trails. Visit the nearby Nauthólsvík geothermal beach (free or small fee in winter) where heated seawater creates a warm lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 15:30-16:00) from Perlan or a hilltop viewpoint. Head back to resort as darkness falls. This is a prime aurora evening - spend 2-3 hours outside on the beachfront with a clear sky watching for the northern lights. Bring hot drinks and warm clothing. Document the aurora with your phone camera using night mode.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort.
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters coffee shop for affordable coffee and pastries, or Sandholt Bakery for quality bread and pastries at reasonable prices (1,500-2,000 ISK for coffee and a meal).
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort. Alternatively, try Reykjavik's Thai restaurant Krua Thai (approx. 2,500-3,000 ISK for a main) - one of the better value sit-down dining options in the city.

day_by_day.notes: Week one complete! Check your budget spending so far. Typical daily budget in Iceland should be around 8,000-12,000 ISK per day (excluding accommodation) when self-catering. Adjust remaining days if needed. January 21st may have slightly more daylight than arrival day as Iceland slowly gains light after the winter solstice.

day_by_day.morning: South Coast adventure - depart early for Iceland's famous South Coast. Drive or take a budget tour toward Vík. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall (free to view, small parking fee) - a stunning 60-meter waterfall you can walk behind in summer, though the path behind may be closed in January due to ice. Still spectacular from the front.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall (free) - one of Iceland's biggest and most beautiful waterfalls. Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views. Then drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík (free) - dramatic basalt column cliffs, sea stacks called Reynisdrangar, and powerful Atlantic waves. WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean here - sneaker waves are deadly.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort before conditions deteriorate. Stop at Dyrhólaey promontory if accessible (free) for views of the coastline and sea arch. Return to resort. The South Coast drive offers excellent aurora viewing on the return journey - pull over safely on a dark stretch of road if the aurora appears.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the car - this is essential as South Coast restaurants are limited and expensive. Hot soup in a thermos is ideal for cold January days.
meals.dinner: Víkurskáli restaurant in Vík if still there (approx. 3,000-4,000 ISK for a main) as a treat, or return to resort for self-catered dinner.

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast is approximately 2-3 hours from Reykjavik. Roads can be challenging in January - check road.is. The black sand beach at Reynisfjara has claimed lives from sneaker waves - maintain a safe distance from the water at all times and never turn your back to the sea. This is a non-negotiable safety warning.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after two consecutive active days. Sleep in late. Visit a local Reykjavik geothermal swimming pool for a relaxing morning soak. Vesturbæjarlaug or Sundhöll Reykjavíkur are central options (approx. 1,000-1,200 ISK). Spend 2-3 hours alternating between the main pool and hot pots - the authentic Icelandic way to spend a winter morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik's art scene for free. Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum - Ásmundarsafn (outdoor sculpture garden is free). Walk through the 101 Reykjavik neighborhood admiring the colorful street art and murals. Browse secondhand shops like Spúútnik on Laugavegur for affordable Icelandic souvenirs and vintage finds.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event. Check Reykjavik Grapevine for listings. Many bars have free live music in the early evening. Alternatively, join a free aurora hunting walk if one is organized by the hostel community. Return to resort for final aurora watch of the evening from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered late breakfast at resort.
meals.lunch: Reykjavik street food - try the food truck scene near Hlemmur Mathöll food hall. Browse the hall for affordable options (soup, sandwiches, or small plates around 1,500-2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort. Comfort food night - make Icelandic skyr pancakes (skyrpönnukökur) for a sweet dinner using supermarket skyr, eggs, and flour.

day_by_day.notes: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall is worth a browse even on a budget - it's a good place to sample small portions of Icelandic specialties without committing to a full expensive restaurant meal. January aurora activity: check spaceweather.com and vedur.is nightly for KP index forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip toward the Reykjanes Peninsula - geothermal wonderland close to the airport. Visit Krýsuvík geothermal area (free) with its colorful boiling mud pools, steaming vents, and sulfuric landscape. The area looks otherworldly in winter with steam rising against the cold sky. Walk the marked paths carefully - ground can be unstable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Gunnuhver hot springs on the Reykjanes Peninsula (free) - Iceland's most powerful hot spring with massive steam columns. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free) - a small footbridge spanning the gap between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, different from Þingvellir but equally symbolic. Drive along the dramatic Reykjanes coastline with its lava fields and lighthouse at Reykjanesviti.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. The Reykjanes Peninsula is close to Keflavik airport area. If your accommodation is beachfront on the Reykjanes Peninsula, this may be a short drive. Spend the evening in a hot pot at the resort if available, or at a public pool. Final serious aurora watch of the main trip - check forecast carefully and stay out as long as possible if KP index is favorable.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the geothermal areas - hot soup, sandwiches, and snacks. Eating among steaming geothermal vents is a memorable Icelandic experience.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort. Use remaining supermarket supplies creatively - pasta with Icelandic smoked lamb (hangikjöt) if available at Bonus.

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula has been volcanically active in recent years with eruptions near Grindavík. Check current volcanic activity status before visiting - some areas may be restricted. The Blue Lagoon is located on the Reykjanes Peninsula but at 12,000-15,000+ ISK is beyond most budget travelers - consider it only if you have remaining budget as a splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik's free outdoor spaces. Visit Elliðaárdalur valley park (free) for a peaceful winter walk along the river - salmon river in summer, icy and beautiful in January. The geothermal greenhouse area nearby may be open for a peek. Walk or take bus to Laugardalur park area - Reykjavik's largest park with botanical garden (free in winter).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Árbær Open Air Museum (Árbæjarsafn) if budget allows (approx. 1,800 ISK) - a collection of historic Icelandic turf houses and buildings relocated to create an outdoor folk museum. Fascinating insight into traditional Icelandic life. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at Laugardalslaug swimming complex (1,200 ISK) with its large hot pots and outdoor pools.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening aurora hunt - this is one of your last chances. If forecast is good (KP 3+, clear skies), drive or walk to the darkest accessible point near your resort. The beachfront away from light pollution is ideal. Spend 2-3 hours watching and photographing. The northern lights can appear as faint green wisps or dramatic dancing curtains of color depending on activity level.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort - use up perishable supermarket supplies.
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch at Reykjavik's Cafe Garðurinn (vegetarian café, approx. 1,500-2,000 ISK for a meal) or self-catered packed lunch.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner on this penultimate full day. Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik Old Harbour offers the famous lobster soup for around 1,800-2,200 ISK - a beloved budget-friendly Reykjavik institution.

day_by_day.notes: Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) is a must-visit budget dining experience in Reykjavik - a rustic harbor hut serving legendary lobster soup and grilled fish skewers at surprisingly affordable prices. It's cash-friendly and a genuine local institution. Get there before the lunchtime rush.

day_by_day.morning: Final full active day - revisit your favorite spots or tick off anything missed. If you haven't visited Þingvellir National Park yet, this is your last chance (free entry). Alternatively, revisit a favorite geothermal pool or hot spring for a final relaxing soak. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs from Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) or Bonus supermarket for affordable Icelandic products (skyr, lava salt, licorice, Brennivín miniatures).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for a final city walk. Photograph Hallgrímskirkja, the Rainbow Street (Skólavörðustígur), and the Old Town area. Visit any museum you missed. Collect any remaining memories of the city before the trip ends. Check out Reykjavik's geothermal heating system infrastructure - the city is heated almost entirely by geothermal energy, a fascinating sustainable achievement.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights vigil. If the forecast is favorable, this is your absolute last chance for aurora viewing. Head to the darkest accessible point. Pack warm drinks and dress in maximum layers. Alternatively, if aurora conditions are poor, enjoy a final evening in Reykjavik - walk Laugavegur street at night when it's atmospheric and lively even in January. Return to resort for packing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort - use final supermarket supplies.
meals.lunch: Final hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur - a fitting budget farewell to Reykjavik (600 ISK).
meals.dinner: Final dinner at resort - self-catered using remaining supplies, or splurge slightly on a farewell meal. Reykjavik's Grillmarkaðurinn has a bar menu with more affordable options, or try Icelandic Fish & Chips near the harbor (approx. 2,500-3,000 ISK) for a solid budget-friendly finale.

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing tonight. Organize receipts and check your overall budget spending. Ensure your passport and flight documents are accessible. Set an early alarm for tomorrow if your departure requires it. Leave a review for the Aegean Bliss Resort if you had a positive experience - it helps other budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If your flight is later in the day, store luggage at the resort or at BSÍ Bus Terminal in Reykjavik. Take a final short walk on the beachfront to say goodbye to Iceland's dramatic coastline. If time allows before checkout, enjoy a final soak in any available hot pot at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time - transfer to Keflavik Airport via Flybus (book in advance, approx. 3,500-4,000 ISK from Reykjavik city center). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5-3 hours before international departure. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Icelandic items (Brennivín schnapps, Icelandic wool products, or volcanic salt are good value in duty-free compared to city shops).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with memories of northern lights, hot springs, dramatic waterfalls, geothermal landscapes, and the unique Icelandic culture. Review your trip highlights and begin planning your next adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at resort using any remaining supplies, or a farewell skyr from the minimarket.
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring packed snacks to the airport. Airport food is expensive - budget 2,000-3,000 ISK if eating at the airport.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Flybus must be booked to match your flight departure time - they run timed services. The journey from Reykjavik to Keflavik Airport takes approximately 45-50 minutes. Budget travelers tip: the cheaper Strætó public bus route 55 connects Reykjavik to Keflavik for about 1,000 ISK but takes longer and runs less frequently. Overall trip budget estimate: accommodation aside, daily expenses of 6,000-10,000 ISK per day are achievable with consistent self-catering and free/low-cost activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a feel for your beachfront surroundings. If energy permits, step outside briefly to scan the sky for the northern lights — January skies in Iceland offer excellent aurora potential.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at Keflavik Airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack from the airport or a 24-hour convenience store near the resort upon arrival. Consider picking up Skyr yogurt and Icelandic flatbread for a simple welcome night snack.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Jet lag and late arrival mean rest is the priority. Confirm your Blue Lagoon and Northern Lights tour bookings before sleeping. January sunrise is around 11:00 AM, so no need for an early alarm.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront to acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape. Explore the immediate surroundings of the Aegean Bliss Resort and enjoy the coastal views. Sunrise won't occur until around 11:00 AM, so make the most of the golden-hour light for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (approximately 15–20 minutes from the Reykjanes Peninsula area). Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy an in-water massage if budget allows. The steam rising against the dark lava fields in January is an otherworldly experience. Book the Comfort Package (mid-range) which includes entrance, silica mud mask, and one drink.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head out for your first Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — a small-group guided tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from light pollution. Your guide will track aurora forecasts in real time and drive to the best viewing locations. Dress in maximum layers.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon for a splurge-lite option
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon's in-water floating bar or the LAVA Restaurant — try the Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa)
meals.dinner: Pre-tour quick dinner at Grillið or a local grill near the resort — try a lamb burger or fish and chips before the evening jeep tour

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon well in advance as slots fill up fast even in January. Northern Lights tours typically depart around 21:00–22:00. Aurora activity depends on cloud cover and solar activity — your guide will have real-time KP index updates.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from the late-night aurora hunt. Enjoy a late breakfast at the resort. Spend the short daylight hours (roughly 11:00 AM to 4:30 PM) exploring the Reykjanes Peninsula — visit the Bridge Between Continents (a walkway spanning the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates) and the Reykjanesviti Lighthouse, Iceland's oldest lighthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gunnuhver Hot Springs — dramatic geothermal mud pools and steam vents on the Reykjanes Peninsula, free to visit. Walk the marked boardwalk paths safely through the bubbling sulfuric landscape. Stop at the nearby Reykjanes Geothermal Power Plant visitor area to learn how Iceland powers itself sustainably.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a quiet dinner and an early evening stroll along the beach scanning the sky for aurora activity independently. Check the Vedur.is aurora forecast app and, if conditions are favorable (KP3+, clear skies), drive just a few minutes from the resort to dark spots along the coast for personal aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or Kaffi Duus in Keflavik — cozy café with pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or Bryggjan Café in Grindavík — traditional Icelandic fish soup in a harbor setting, budget-friendly
meals.dinner: Salthúsið Restaurant in Grindavík — fresh local seafood at mid-range prices, try the pan-fried Arctic char

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver Hot Springs are free and easily accessible. Stick to marked paths — the ground around geothermal vents can be dangerously thin. January temperatures average -1°C to 4°C, with strong coastal winds — windproof layers are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Drive toward Reykjavik (approximately 45 minutes from the resort area). Begin the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour — explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, lamb, and Icelandic hot dogs. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja Church and Harpa Concert Hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik independently after the tour. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for an affordable deep dive into Viking and Icelandic history (around 2,500 ISK entry). Stroll Laugavegur Street — Iceland's main shopping street — for local wool sweaters (lopapeysa), design goods, and souvenirs. Visit the Reykjavik City Library's free exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's evening scene. Visit a local geothermal public pool — Sundhöll Reykjavíkur or Laugardalslaug (entry ~1,000 ISK) — for a true local experience of outdoor hot pots in the winter cold. Afterward, enjoy dinner in the city before driving back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the Food & Culture Walking Tour, supplemented by Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Reykjavik's famous hot dog stand (under 500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur — modern Icelandic cuisine using traditional recipes, mid-range pricing. Try the 'whole lamb's head' or skyr cheesecake.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour in advance. Tours typically run 3 hours. Laugavegur Street shops close around 18:00–20:00. Public geothermal pools are a beloved local tradition — bring a swimsuit and towel.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Golden Circle — Iceland's most iconic day-trip route (roughly 1.5–2 hours from the resort). First stop: Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá gorge canyon as daylight begins around 11:00 AM. The rift valley is dramatic even under snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls, partially frozen in January and absolutely stunning. Frozen spray and ice formations make this a winter highlight.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort via Route 35/36. On the drive back, stop at Kerið Volcanic Crater — a vivid red and ochre crater lake (entry ~400 ISK). If aurora forecast is favorable, pull over on a dark rural road on the return drive for spontaneous northern lights viewing. Arrive back at the resort by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Geysir Center cafeteria — hearty lamb soup and sandwiches, affordable and warming
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Tomato Farm Restaurant near Selfoss — unique greenhouse dining experience where everything is made with their own tomatoes. Mid-range, reservation recommended.

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from the resort. Roads in January can be icy — check road.is before departure. Rent a 4WD vehicle if not already arranged. Bring microspikes/yaktrax for icy walking surfaces at waterfalls and geysers.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day at the resort. Sleep in and enjoy a full breakfast. Use the morning to review photos, plan remaining days, and relax at the resort's facilities. If the resort has a hot tub or pool, enjoy it during the late morning. January light is precious — take a short beachfront walk during the brief daylight window.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approximately 1.5 hours from the resort). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this natural hot spring sits in a geothermal field with small geysers erupting nearby. Soak in the 38–40°C natural pool surrounded by steam and snow — a truly authentic Icelandic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort. Stop for dinner in Selfoss — a charming town en route. If aurora conditions are strong (check Vedur.is), park on a dark road outside town for aurora photography. The Secret Lagoon area around Flúðir is also an excellent dark-sky zone — consider lingering if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Light snack at the resort or packed lunch for the drive
meals.dinner: Kaffi Krús in Selfoss — cozy local restaurant with Icelandic comfort food including lamb stew and fresh fish, very mid-range friendly

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is approximately 3,500 ISK — significantly more affordable than Blue Lagoon. Towel rental available on-site. The geothermal field around the lagoon has active small geysers — stay on marked paths. Book ahead during peak aurora season.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the South Coast toward Vík (approximately 2.5 hours from the resort). First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — walk behind the curtain of falling water (may be icy/closed in January — check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall — climb the 527 steps to the top for panoramic views of the snow-covered South Coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík — dramatic basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks), powerful Atlantic waves, and jet-black volcanic sand. Explore the Reynisfjall cave basalt columns. Exercise extreme caution — 'sneaker waves' are deadly here. Never turn your back on the ocean. Drive into Vík village and explore the red-roofed Vík church perched on the hillside.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse in or near Vík for the night (pre-booked), or drive back toward the resort if preferred (long drive). If staying near Vík, take an evening walk to the black beach for aurora hunting — the sea stacks and black sand make for extraordinary aurora photography backdrops. The area has minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Skógarfoss Café at the waterfall base — hot soup and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — local fish and lamb dishes with ocean views, mid-range pricing

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~5–6 hours total driving). Start early to maximize the 5.5 hours of daylight. Roads on the South Coast can be icy — 4WD essential. Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the waterfall is often closed in winter due to ice — check ahead. Reynisfjara waves are extremely dangerous — maintain a 30-meter safety distance.

day_by_day.morning: From Vík (or resort if you returned), drive to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (approximately 2.5 hours east of Vík). Witness enormous icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier floating serenely in the lagoon. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating a surreal ice landscape. Walk to the adjacent Diamond Beach where translucent ice chunks wash up on black sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Fjallsárlón Glacier Lagoon — smaller and less visited than Jökulsárlón, with equally stunning reflections of the Vatnajökull glacier. Walk the shoreline and enjoy the profound silence of Iceland's largest national park. If conditions allow, consider a short snowshoe walk on the glacier edge with a certified guide (bookable locally).
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back west. Stop at the Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon (near Kirkjubæjarklaustur) if road conditions permit — a dramatic 100-meter deep, 2 km long canyon. Return to the resort or a midway guesthouse. If driving the full route back, keep eyes on the sky — the South Coast offers outstanding aurora viewing away from all light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Vík guesthouse or café
meals.lunch: Glacier Lagoon Café (Jökulsárlón) — hot drinks and light meals with iceberg views
meals.dinner: Hótel Skaftá restaurant in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — hearty Icelandic lamb and fish dishes, mid-range

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 380 km from the resort — this is Iceland's longest day trip. Consider an overnight stay in the East to reduce driving pressure. Seals are commonly spotted in the lagoon year-round. The ice on Diamond Beach can be slippery — wear grippy footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the resort if you stayed overnight on the South Coast. Rest and recover from the long driving days. Enjoy a late breakfast and the resort amenities. Use the morning to do laundry, recharge camera batteries, and back up photos. Take a slow walk along the beachfront in the precious midday light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula's lesser-known geothermal gems: the Seltún Geothermal Area in Krýsuvík — colorful sulfuric hot springs, bubbling mud pools, and steaming vents set against a vivid landscape of yellow, red, and orange mineral deposits. Entry is free. Nearby, walk to Lake Kleifarvatn — Iceland's largest lake on the peninsula, hauntingly beautiful in winter with potential ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour (book a second session for a different route/location than Day 2). January offers multiple aurora opportunities — experienced guides will target different dark-sky zones. The Reykjanes Peninsula's interior and highland edges are prime aurora territory. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or Kaffi Duus in Keflavik for a warming bowl of soup
meals.dinner: Víkin Seafood Restaurant in Hafnarfjörður — fresh Atlantic seafood in a Viking-themed setting, mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Seltún/Krýsuvík is approximately 30 minutes from the resort — an easy half-day excursion. The geothermal area has boardwalks but can be icy — microspikes recommended. Lake Kleifarvatn is known for its eerie atmosphere — a perfect moody winter photography location.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2–2.5 hours from the resort). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier volcano that inspired Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Stop at Arnarstapi and Hellnar for dramatic coastal cliffs, lava arch formations, and seabird colonies. The glacier looming above in winter is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the Snæfellsnes Peninsula: visit Kirkjufell Mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain, shaped like a pointed church. In January, the mountain is snow-capped and the nearby Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall may be partially frozen, creating extraordinary photographic compositions. Explore Grundarfjörður village for local culture.
day_by_day.evening: The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is one of Iceland's top aurora-viewing regions due to minimal light pollution and dramatic landscape backdrops. Stay in the area overnight at a local guesthouse (pre-booked) and spend the evening aurora hunting independently around Kirkjufell — the mountain with northern lights overhead is an iconic Iceland shot.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið Café in Hellnar — legendary homemade soup and cakes in a cliffside setting, very mid-range
meals.dinner: Bjargarsteinn Mathús in Grundarfjörður — local seafood and lamb with views of Kirkjufell, mid-range

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day excursion — consider an overnight stay to reduce driving and maximize aurora opportunities. The peninsula road (Route 54) is generally well-maintained but check road.is. The Snæfellsjökull glacier summit requires a guided tour — do not attempt independently in winter.

day_by_day.morning: If overnight on Snæfellsnes, explore the northern side of the peninsula in the morning: visit Búðir Black Church — a tiny, iconic black wooden church against white snow and the glacier. Walk the nearby Búðahraun lava field. Continue to Ytri Tunga beach — a seal colony beach where harbor seals bask on rocks year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward the resort (2–2.5 hours). Stop in Borgarnes on the return journey — visit the Settlement Center of Iceland, an interactive museum telling the story of Iceland's first Viking settlers through immersive audio-visual exhibits (approximately 2,500 ISK). Enjoy the town's peaceful harbor atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the resort by late afternoon/early evening. Enjoy a relaxing dinner at or near the resort. Spend the evening in the resort's hot tub or facilities, reflecting on the trip so far. Do a final check of remaining days and confirm any outstanding bookings.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast on Snæfellsnes
meals.lunch: Hyrnan Restaurant in Borgarnes — casual Icelandic café with soup and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Resort dinner or a local restaurant near the Aegean Bliss Resort — try fresh langoustine (Icelandic lobster) if available

day_by_day.notes: Ytri Tunga seal beach is free to visit — seals are most active during low tide. The Settlement Center in Borgarnes is excellent for historical context and well worth the entry fee. Return to the resort early enough to rest before the final days.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike — note that Landmannalaugar's highland roads (F-roads) are typically inaccessible in January due to snow and ice. Instead, enjoy the best available alternative: visit the Hrunalaug Hot Spring near Flúðir (a hidden natural hot pool, free to visit, set in a lava cave) combined with a scenic winter hike through the Þórsmörk valley lowland trails accessible in winter with proper gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seljavallalaug Geothermal Pool — one of Iceland's oldest swimming pools (built 1923), nestled in a mountain valley and fed by natural hot springs. A 15-minute walk through a snowy mountain gorge leads to this hidden gem. Entry is free. The pool sits at approximately 25°C — cooler than other hot springs but deeply atmospheric in winter. Combine with a short hike in the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights opportunity — drive to a pre-scouted dark location on the Reykjanes Peninsula or near the resort. Set up for dedicated aurora photography using a tripod. Alternatively, book a final aurora jeep tour if the previous tours had poor conditions. Celebrate the penultimate evening with a special dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the hiking day — Icelandic lamb sandwiches and Skyr from a local supermarket
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at VOX Restaurant in Reykjavik or Íslenski Barinn (The Icelandic Bar) — traditional Icelandic feast with lamb, fish, and Brennivín schnapps, mid-range splurge

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar is only accessible July–September. Seljavallalaug is a worthy January alternative — the 15-minute trail can be icy, bring microspikes. The pool is maintained by volunteers and has a small changing hut. Bring your own towel. Check Vedur.is obsessively on this evening for the best aurora conditions of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up for one last sunrise (around 10:45 AM) walk along the beachfront of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Take final photos of the dramatic Icelandic coastal landscape. Pack and check out of the resort. If time permits before airport transfer, make one final visit to the Blue Lagoon's on-site café for a farewell coffee overlooking the geothermal waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Keflavik International Airport (15–20 minutes from the resort area). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Pick up Icelandic souvenirs at the airport: local chocolate, Skyr, Brennivín, lopapeysa wool goods, and lava salt.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of northern lights, geothermal wonders, volcanic landscapes, and Icelandic culture. Keep your camera ready on the plane — aurora sightings from aircraft at altitude are not uncommon on northbound flights in January.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor it
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon café farewell coffee and pastry, or a quick meal at Keflavik Airport
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and arrange resort checkout and airport transfer the evening before. Keflavik Airport has excellent duty-free shopping — Icelandic wool products are significantly cheaper at local shops than at the airport, so buy souvenirs in Reykjavik if possible. Iceland's 11% VAT refund is available for purchases over 6,000 ISK — collect your refund forms at the airport. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to maximize your chances of seeing the lights dance across the sky. Hot chocolate and blankets provided.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and the surreal experience of bathing outdoors in steaming 38°C waters surrounded by black lava fields. Book the Comfort package for best value.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers in a stunning rural setting. A truly local and affordable alternative.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fresh-caught Arctic char, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbor district with knowledgeable local guides.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's dramatic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The hike offers breathtaking views of obsidian lava fields, steaming vents, and vivid mineral-streaked mountains unlike anywhere else on Earth.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a late welcome drink and light charcuterie board prepared by the resort. Check in, unwind in your beachfront suite, and settle in for the night.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome charcuterie and champagne reception at Aegean Bliss Resort

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. The resort should be notified of the late arrival in advance so staff are ready and a warm welcome amenity is prepared. Keep the first night light – rest is essential after the long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely full Icelandic breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant overlooking the beachfront. Take a slow morning walk along the coastal shoreline to breathe in the Arctic air and acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-famous Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa, just a short drive from the resort. Indulge in the milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Book the premium Retreat Spa package, which includes in-water massage, a silica mud mask ritual, algae mask treatment, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lagoon reserved for premium guests only.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at the Blue Lagoon's Lava Restaurant, one of Iceland's most celebrated fine-dining venues, built into a 800-year-old lava field. Enjoy a tasting menu featuring Icelandic langoustine, Arctic char, and skyr-based desserts with curated wine pairings. Return to the resort for a nightcap and watch for northern lights from your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – smoked salmon, skyr, fresh bread, local cheeses, and hot beverages
meals.lunch: Light bites and smoothies at the Blue Lagoon Lagoon Bar (enjoyed while floating in the geothermal waters)
meals.dinner: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon – multi-course tasting menu with Icelandic seafood and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa package well in advance as slots fill up quickly, especially in peak winter season. Bring a waterproof hair tie and plan for at least 3–4 hours at the lagoon. Sunset in January occurs around 16:00, so afternoon light will be limited.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, join the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour departing from the capital. Explore Iceland's vibrant city through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, lamb soup, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the Settlement Exhibition museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik independently. Browse the luxury boutiques and design shops along Laugavegur street. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall, an architectural gem on the harbor, and enjoy a hot chocolate at a chic café. Explore the National Museum of Iceland for deeper cultural context.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep – join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness, far from city light pollution. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts to chase the best viewing locations. Enjoy hot cocoa and Icelandic kleina pastries under the stars while waiting for the aurora borealis to appear.

meals.breakfast: Icelandic breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour; supplement with a sit-down lunch at Messinn Restaurant – famous for its pan-fried Icelandic fish dishes
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik – Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering New Nordic cuisine with locally foraged and seasonal ingredients; pair with the chef's tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: The Northern Lights Hunt typically departs around 20:00–21:00 and lasts 3–4 hours. Dress in extreme cold-weather layers – thermal base, fleece mid-layer, and waterproof outer shell. The resort can arrange a luxury vehicle to and from Reykjavik for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a private guided Golden Circle tour. Begin at Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic Almannagjá canyon with a private naturalist guide explaining Iceland's geological and parliamentary history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area to witness the Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 30 meters into the air. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, one of Europe's most powerful waterfalls, partially frozen in January creating a spectacular icy spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. Stop for dinner at Friðheimar, a unique greenhouse restaurant where tomatoes are grown year-round using geothermal energy. Enjoy tomato-based cuisine in a warm, enchanting atmosphere. Back at the resort, relax in the hot tub on your beachfront suite terrace and scan the sky for northern lights.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed picnic lunch prepared by the resort, enjoyed at Þingvellir National Park
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant – tomato soup, fresh salads, pasta, and house-made tomato beer in a geothermal greenhouse setting

day_by_day.notes: January roads on the Golden Circle can be icy. Ensure the private tour uses a 4WD vehicle with experienced winter drivers. Wear ice cleats (available at the resort or rental shops) for walking at Þingvellir and Gullfoss. Daylight is approximately 5–6 hours in January, so maximize outdoor time between 11:00–16:00.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning at the resort. Enjoy the resort's spa facilities, including a geothermal pool, steam room, and signature Arctic massage treatment. Take a late morning stroll along the beachfront and enjoy the dramatic winter seascape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula for a private afternoon excursion. Visit the mystical Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth'). Explore the dramatic Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the haunting basalt columns at Lóndrangar sea stacks.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a premium seafood restaurant in the Snæfellsnes area, such as Hotel Búðir's restaurant – a legendary remote luxury hotel with one of Iceland's finest kitchens, serving fresh local catch with panoramic views of the glacier. Return to the resort and join a second Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep if aurora activity is forecast.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort spa café – smoked salmon open sandwiches, Icelandic yogurt bowls, and herbal teas
meals.dinner: Hotel Búðir Restaurant – refined Icelandic cuisine featuring local lamb, fresh fish, and foraged herbs in an intimate candlelit setting

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes Peninsula is approximately 2–2.5 hours from the resort. A private driver is strongly recommended for this excursion due to winter road conditions. Check road conditions at road.is before departing. The peninsula is one of Iceland's best aurora viewing spots due to minimal light pollution.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for the South Coast. Visit the iconic Seljalandsfoss waterfall where you can walk behind the curtain of water (weather permitting in winter). Continue to the equally stunning Skógafoss waterfall and climb the 527 steps to the top viewing platform for panoramic views of the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the haunting black sand beaches of Reynisfjara near Vík. Marvel at the dramatic basalt column formations and the roaring Atlantic surf. Visit the charming village of Vík and the iconic Reyniskirkja church perched on the hillside. Stop at the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (weather and road conditions permitting) to see floating blue icebergs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at Sudur-Vík Restaurant in Vík, known for its warm atmosphere and hearty Icelandic cuisine featuring local lamb and seafood. Return to the resort. If northern lights are active, stop at a dark roadside location en route for stargazing and aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – grab-and-go option arranged by the resort
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from the resort, enjoyed with views of Reynisfjara black sand beach
meals.dinner: Sudur-Vík Restaurant – Icelandic lamb stew, pan-seared Arctic char, and local berry desserts

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast is a full-day excursion of approximately 300–400 km round trip. A private luxury 4WD with an experienced driver-guide is essential. Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves – stay well back from the waterline and heed all warning signs. Return journey in complete darkness, so aurora spotting en route is possible.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint rest and recovery day. Enjoy a slow morning with a spa treatment at the resort – book the signature 90-minute volcanic stone massage. Read, relax, and enjoy the dramatic winter seascape from your beachfront suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir, Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool offers a more intimate and local experience. Soak in the naturally heated 38–40°C waters surrounded by geysers and steaming vents in a serene countryside setting.
day_by_day.afternoon_note: The Secret Lagoon is approximately 1.5 hours from the resort – arrange a private transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a refined private in-suite dining experience. The resort's chef prepares a bespoke 5-course Icelandic tasting menu served in your beachfront suite with curated wine pairings. Watch for northern lights from your private terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at the resort restaurant
meals.lunch: Warm soup and Icelandic pastries at the Secret Lagoon's on-site café
meals.dinner: Private in-suite 5-course chef's tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort – langoustine bisque, smoked lamb tartare, pan-seared cod, Icelandic cheese board, and skyr panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange the private in-suite dining experience with the resort concierge at least 24 hours in advance. The Secret Lagoon is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Bring a robe and slippers from the resort for maximum comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter tour of Iceland's volcanic highlands and glaciers. Depart from a nearby helipad for a breathtaking aerial perspective of Iceland's otherworldly landscape – soaring over lava fields, glaciers, geothermal vents, and remote mountain ranges. Land on a glacier for a champagne toast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon exploring the resort's private coastal grounds. Take an ATV or snowmobile tour (if offered by the resort) along the beachfront. Alternatively, enjoy a private yoga session overlooking the ocean arranged by the resort's wellness team.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep – second dedicated aurora hunting excursion with expert guides. Tonight, venture to a different location with optimal aurora forecast conditions. Enjoy warm beverages and Icelandic treats under the dark sky.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the helicopter tour
meals.lunch: Gourmet in-flight picnic hamper provided during the helicopter excursion, enjoyed on the glacier
meals.dinner: Grillhúsið (The Grill House) – a premium steakhouse in the Reykjanes area featuring Icelandic grass-fed beef, local lamb chops, and an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours are subject to weather conditions and must be booked well in advance through a reputable operator such as Norðurflug or Íslandsflug. Dress in warm layers for the glacier landing. The evening Northern Lights Hunt is a second attempt to maximize aurora viewing chances during the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike. Trek through Iceland's dramatic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands. The winter landscape adds an ethereal quality to the already surreal terrain. A private guide leads the hike through steaming fumaroles, obsidian lava fields, and snow-dusted peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the Landmannalaugar hot spring pool and reward yourself with a long, restorative soak in the naturally heated geothermal waters surrounded by snow-capped mountains. The contrast of warm water and cold Arctic air is an unforgettable sensory experience. Enjoy hot soup and thermos drinks brought by your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort. Due to the long day, dinner will be at the resort's signature restaurant. Enjoy a hearty Icelandic dinner featuring slow-roasted lamb and root vegetables, followed by an early night to rest.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Gourmet thermos lunch provided by the private guide at Landmannalaugar – lamb soup, rye bread, smoked trout, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant – slow-roasted Icelandic lamb shoulder, roasted root vegetables, and skyr cheesecake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in winter requires a highly experienced guide and a super-jeep with extreme off-road capability. The F-roads to the Highlands are only accessible in winter via organized super-jeep tours. Wear full waterproof gear and bring a swimsuit for the hot spring. This is a physically demanding day – wear appropriate hiking boots with crampons.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort. Sleep in and enjoy a long breakfast. Book a private geothermal facial and body wrap treatment at the resort spa using Icelandic volcanic minerals and algae extracts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private ice cave tour near Þórsmörk or the Katla volcano glacier. A super-jeep transfers you to the glacier where a certified glacier guide leads you into a stunning natural ice cave with vivid blue and turquoise ice formations. Don crampons and a helmet for a safe and awe-inspiring underground adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the penultimate days of the trip with a special dinner at Óx Restaurant in Reykjavik – an ultra-exclusive 12-seat omakase-style restaurant by the team behind Dill, offering one of Iceland's most extraordinary dining experiences. Reservation must be booked months in advance.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the glacier tour departure point – fish soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavik – intimate 12-course omakase tasting menu celebrating Icelandic ingredients with theatrical presentation and premium wine or sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours are only available in winter (November–March) when the ice is stable. Always use a certified glacier guide and reputable operator. The Óx Restaurant reservation is extremely difficult to secure – book as far in advance as possible, ideally when planning the trip. Private luxury transfer to and from Reykjavik is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Reykjanes Peninsula UNESCO Global Geopark – explore the dramatic volcanic landscape right on the Reykjanes Ridge. Visit the Bridge Between Continents where you can literally walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Explore the Gunnuhver hot spring area with its powerful mud pools and steam vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Blue Lagoon for a second visit – this time book the exclusive Silica Hotel private lagoon experience or the Retreat Spa's signature Aqua Vitae ritual, a 2-hour immersive in-water wellness journey. Enjoy the full spa menu at a more leisurely pace than the first visit.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell eve dinner at the resort's finest table. Enjoy a bespoke chef's menu prepared specifically for your group, celebrating the Icelandic culinary journey with the finest local ingredients. Pair with a curated selection of Icelandic craft spirits and wines. Afterward, take a final late-night walk along the beachfront hoping for one last northern lights display.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: In-water dining at the Blue Lagoon – enjoy a glass of sparkling wine and a fresh seafood platter while floating in the geothermal waters
meals.dinner: Bespoke farewell chef's dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – 6-course celebration menu with Icelandic caviar, langoustine, lamb, and a signature skyr dessert creation

day_by_day.notes: The Gunnuhver hot spring area is close to where the Reykjanes eruptions have been active in recent years – check local advisories before visiting. The resort concierge should be notified in advance to arrange the special farewell dinner. Request a table by the window for beachfront views.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day – begin with a sunrise walk (around 11:00 in January) along the beachfront to soak in the last moments of Iceland's magical winter light. Pack any souvenirs and gifts purchased during the trip. Visit the resort's gift shop for premium Icelandic products – lopapeysa wool sweaters, lava salt, and local skincare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final excursion: private whale watching tour from Reykjavik harbor (winter season offers sightings of humpback whales and minke whales). Wrap up in luxury blankets provided on board a premium vessel with a knowledgeable marine biologist guide. Hot drinks and snacks served on board.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik – a beloved restaurant celebrating traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined with modern technique. Enjoy dishes like 'the whole cod' and traditional lamb head prepared with contemporary flair. Return to the resort for a final night's rest.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort – savor every last bite of Icelandic skyr, smoked salmon, and fresh bread
meals.lunch: Hot smoked lamb sandwiches and Icelandic fish soup at a cozy Reykjavik café such as Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur, Reykjavik – traditional Icelandic recipes with a contemporary twist; try the lamb head, fermented shark, and rye bread ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching tours operate year-round but are subject to sea conditions. January can be rough – check with the operator the morning of the excursion. Dress in extreme cold-weather gear for the boat. Begin packing this evening and confirm departure transfer with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final breakfast at the resort. Check out and arrange private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. If time permits before the flight, make one last stop at the Blue Lagoon airport location for a final soak and spa treatment before departure – the Blue Lagoon is conveniently located minutes from the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of northern lights, geothermal wonders, dramatic landscapes, and world-class cuisine. Carry home memories of Iceland's raw, otherworldly beauty.
day_by_day.evening: In transit – homeward bound.

meals.breakfast: Final full Icelandic breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – a proper send-off with all the favorites from the past two weeks
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon café or Keflavík airport premium lounge dining
meals.dinner: On board flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. The Blue Lagoon stop is only feasible if your flight departs after 14:00. Confirm all luggage is within airline weight limits – Icelandic wool products and souvenirs can add significant weight. Leave a generous tip for the resort staff who made the stay exceptional.
